title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (December 2026 data), 9:00 a.m. ET — the annual-scorecard edition: the only one of the twelve that reframes to the calendar year
source: NEWS: the publisher's own standing rule, read verbatim out of TWO further S&P Dow Jones Indices press releases fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this initial research — documents no sibling lane had read: the December-2025-data edition (press.spglobal.com/2026-02-24-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-December-2025, HTTP 200, 97,759 bytes) and the November-2025-data edition (the 2026-01-27 slug, HTTP 200, 98,097 bytes). Both carry the identical sentence the case-shiller-hpi-2027-03-30 lane read out of three other editions on 2026-09-08: "The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET." Five releases now, five agreements. Independently reproduced by weekday arithmetic — February 2027's Tuesdays are the 2nd, 9th, 16th and 23rd, so 2027-02-23 is the last — and the stated two-month reporting lag puts DECEMBER 2026 data on it, which the 2026-02-24 analog edition confirms directly by reporting December 2025 on the last Tuesday of February 2026. Filed estimate on taxonomy, NOT on date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs is (IR|CAL|BLS|FED|PJM|SEC|TSY|OCC|BEA|CENSUS|ISM|CB|UMICH|FHFA) and has no member for an index provider's own standing publication rule — the same gap every S&P DJI and Russell entry on this calendar records, and a discovering lane may not self-confirm. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the case-shiller-hpi-2027-03-30 initial research (2026-09-08) as its predecessor edition; researched 2026-09-09, and the proposal file is now shadowed by this canonical one. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED TO THE PROPOSAL, VERIFIED BY A TREATMENT-AND-CONTROL FETCH: this is not merely the predecessor that collapses the 03-30 print's forecast distance — it is THE ANNUAL SCORECARD, and it is the only one of the twelve editions in a year that is. The December-2025-data edition (2026-02-24) reframes its entire ANALYSIS section to the calendar year in the publisher's own words -- "With December's results, we can now assess 2025's full-year performance in historical context" -- and reports "National home prices grew just 1.3% for the year, the weakest full-year gain since 2011", an H1 +2.6% / H2 -1.3% split, all 20 metros negative in the back half, and a city league table "for the full year". The November-2025-data control edition (2026-01-27), fetched in the same pass, contains NO full-year framing at all: "full-year", "full year", "for the year" and "in historical context" are all absent. So the February edition is where this index's number leaves the housing pages and becomes the year's headline. TWO MEASURED CONSEQUENCES. (1) December is the SEASONAL FLOOR of the NSA calendar -- median m/m -0.064pp with 59.0% of Decembers negative (n=39, FRED CSUSHPINSA 1987-01 -> 2026-06), the deepest of the only three negative-median months (Oct -0.001/51.3%, Nov -0.005/53.8%) -- and its Oct-Nov-Dec reference window sums to -0.070pp, the coldest of all twelve. This is the edition where the m/m is worst as signal and a full-year figure is what actually travels. (2) The 2026 scorecard is already mostly determined and it argues AGAINST a repeat of the "weakest since 2011" framing: the H1-2026 carry is +2.944pp (Jun-2026 336.663 / Dec-2025 327.035), so full-year 2026 lands at or below 2025's current-vintage +1.15% only if H2-2026 runs <= -1.743%, which is 7 of 39 years, and turns negative only if H2 <= -2.860%, which is 5 of 39 and every instance is 2007-2011 or 2022. Impact low and symbols: [] on the measured basis every sibling housing entry records: 0 hits for any housing / house-price / macro keying in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md or docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-09).
